summary: Dry-run #2 system-level acceptance against ba.json's 44 ACs and 17 edge cases. The spine is structurally wired (Cart -> Checkout -> Order -> Payment paths exist, INFLIGHT idempotency race-fix is present, Order is the sole writer of order.status, contracts.json is internally consistent post-refactor). However three system-level gaps prevent a clean end-to-end pass: (1) the §7.1 customer journey breaks at Checkout.commit step 4b and Cart.read fan-out because inventory.stock.bulk-read is a 501 STUB while both callers issue the call -- a spine-load-bearing stub that knocks AC-CHK-004 (INSUFFICIENT_STOCK) and the cart-availability story off the rails; (2) every Checkout.commit successful path generates a fresh uuid.New() for orders.id rather than using the client-supplied Idempotency-Key (REV-ORDER-001 in Order is the upstream defect, but the system-level effect is that AC-CHK-009 idempotent retry returns a NEW order on the second POST instead of the original, breaking ba.json AC line 200 'Exactly one order is created'); (3) the frontend customer journey AC (ba.json line 300) cannot complete because /api/proxy/checkout/commit and /api/proxy/payment/simulate are missing dedicated route handlers, so the Idempotency-Key header never reaches the Checkout backend -- duplicate Place-Order taps create duplicate orders. None of these are duplicates of Reviewer-L1 per-component findings: (1) is a cross-component contract gap (consumer expects FULL, provider ships STUB), (2) is the system-level effect of REV-ORDER-001 visible at the Checkout->Order boundary which Reviewer-L1 did not file under that lens, (3) crosses Frontend->Checkout. AC trace: 16 covered_full, 8 covered_partial, 13 covered_stub, 7 uncovered. Edge case trace: 4 covered_full, 4 covered_partial, 6 covered_stub, 3 uncovered. Routes to Tech-Designer (re-scope inventory.stock.bulk-read into Wave A) and Dev (fix orders.id derivation + frontend Idempotency-Key forwarding).

criteria_unmet.title: inventory.stock.bulk-read 501 STUB blocks Checkout step 4b and Cart.read enrichment, knocking AC-CHK-004 (INSUFFICIENT_STOCK) and CART-002 stock-aware quantity edits off-spine
criteria_unmet.evidence: backend/services/inventory/app/inventory/handler_stock_bulk_read.go:12 STUB; backend/services/checkout/app/checkout/client_inventory.go:51 calls /api/v1/inventory/stock/bulk-read; backend/services/cart/app/cart/client_inventory.go:45 calls same. Cart's QA-L1 fan-out finding (F-003) and Inventory's QA-L1 STUB-list both surface this individually; the SYSTEM-LEVEL effect is that two BA acceptance criteria depend on a third party that returns 501. Distinct from per-component scope-stub framing because both Cart and Checkout are FULL endpoints whose declared dependency is unmet.
criteria_unmet.rationale: Either (a) re-scope inventory.stock.bulk-read into Wave A so the STUB becomes FULL, or (b) re-scope Checkout step 4b + Cart.read enrichment to skip stock-bulk-read in MVP and rely solely on inventory.reservation.create for the stock check (CHK-004 then surfaces via reservation.create's INSUFFICIENT_STOCK return rather than at preview-time). Option (a) closes the gap; option (b) reduces fidelity but is a smaller diff.

criteria_unmet.title: Order.create-from-checkout uses uuid.New() for orders.id instead of req.IdempotencyKey, breaking AC-CHK-009 idempotent order replay
criteria_unmet.evidence: backend/services/order/app/order/handler_create_from_checkout.go:42 `orderID := uuid.New().String()`. cross-cutting.idempotency.internal_orderId_rule in contracts.json mandates orders.id == request.idempotencyKey so duplicate INSERT raises a PK violation that the handler treats as replay. As shipped, every Checkout retry creates a NEW order id even with the same idempotency key. SYSTEM-LEVEL view: AC-CHK-009 line 200 of ba.json says 'Exactly one order is created' -- this fails when Checkout's INFLIGHT row is somehow lost (e.g., DB pruning, or distinct INFLIGHT rows landing on different replicas after a checkout-side restart) because Order has no second-line PK guard. Reviewer-L1 filed REV-ORDER-001 routing to Dev for the per-component fix; we re-cite it at the system level because the Checkout->Order contract boundary is the load-bearing surface here.
criteria_unmet.rationale: Apply the REV-ORDER-001 fix: use req.IdempotencyKey (UUID v7 from Checkout) as orders.id; on PK conflict (PG 23505), SELECT existing row and return the same envelope with HTTP 200. This is a 5-line fix in handler_create_from_checkout.go.

criteria_unmet.title: Payment service is missing the outbox_relay goroutine, so events.payment.completed/failed/expired never reach Kafka -> Order.consumer never receives them -> orders never transition out of PENDING_PAYMENT
criteria_unmet.evidence: backend/services/payment/app/payment — no outbox_relay.go file (QA-PAY F-01 confirmed); main.go starts only the sweeper, not a relay goroutine. backend/services/payment/access has OutboxStorage interface but no caller drains it. Order's payment.completed consumer (consumer.go) is FULL and waits on Kafka topic ecom.payment.events but no producer ships events to that topic. SYSTEM-LEVEL view: BA success_conditions §7.1 (1) requires 'simulates a successful mock payment ... and lands on orderDetail showing status=PAID with reserved stock converted to sold' -- this end-state is unreachable. The user lands on orderSuccess (frontend route based on payment-service response) but orderDetail still shows PENDING_PAYMENT because Order never received the event. Distinct from the per-component QA-PAY F-01 because Reviewer-L1 framed it as 'rows accumulate'; the system-level framing is 'the spine never completes the PAID transition'.
criteria_unmet.rationale: Implement payment/app/payment/outbox_relay.go (5s tick, ListPending LIMIT 100, produce to Kafka via common/kafka.Producer, MarkPublished); wire goroutine startup in main.go alongside the sweeper. Pattern is already implemented in catalog (with the Rev-L1 REV-CATALOG-002 panic-recover advisory) and order has the storage interface but is missing the goroutine too -- the full fix should also wire order's outbox publisher (REV-ORDER-004).

criteria_unmet.title: Frontend Idempotency-Key for /api/checkout/commit and /api/payment/simulate is dropped at the proxy boundary, so duplicate Place-Order taps create duplicate orders even after l2-fail-002 is fixed
criteria_unmet.evidence: frontend/app/checkout/CheckoutCommitButton.tsx:23 POSTs to /api/proxy/checkout/commit with Idempotency-Key header. No frontend/app/api/checkout/commit/route.ts exists; the [...path] catch-all (frontend/app/api/proxy/[...path]/route.ts:57-77) does NOT forward the Idempotency-Key header to the backend. Same gap on payment/simulate. Reviewer-L1 REV-FRONTEND-WEB-001 filed this as a per-component finding. SYSTEM-LEVEL framing: the frontend->checkout->order contract chain has THREE redundant idempotency layers (frontend body field, proxy header, checkout TryClaimOrLookup) and ZERO are connected end-to-end without dedicated route handlers. Even after l2-fail-002 is fixed (Order using request.idempotencyKey as orders.id), the frontend never sends one, so two rapid Place-Order taps result in two distinct INFLIGHT rows on Checkout side and two distinct orderIds on Order side.
criteria_unmet.rationale: Create frontend/app/api/checkout/commit/route.ts and frontend/app/api/payment/simulate/route.ts as dedicated handlers per TD route_handler_topology; read body field idempotencyKey + Idempotency-Key header; forward as 'Idempotency-Key' on the downstream call. Per Rev-L1 REV-FRONTEND-WEB-001.

system_level_concerns_distinct_from_rev_: Spine break #1 — inventory.stock.bulk-read STUB blocks Checkout step 4b and Cart.read fan-out (Rev-L1 framed as per-component scope reduction; system-level effect is two FULL endpoints depending on a STUB).

Spine break #2 — Order.create-from-checkout uuid.New() means the cross-cutting idempotency rule (orderId == idempotencyKey) is broken at the Checkout->Order contract surface (Rev-L1 filed REV-ORDER-001 as per-component; system view names the cross-component contract as load-bearing).
